mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < previous 6-month average) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% AND HOUST < 6-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during an NBER-defined recession.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months, combined with accelerating industrial production growth (INDPRO > 0.5% MoM for three months), signals a late-cycle economy where labor market tightness and capacity expansion precede equity valuation corrections.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO > 0.5% MoM for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the mechanism does not fire during a subsequent recession.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% per month signals a meaningful contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a supply-chain normalization period.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in nonfarm payrolls growth (PAYEMS month-on-month change falling by at least 150k from previous month) signals labor market cooling that precedes equity market weakness, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM change drops by ≥150k from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a subsequent recession.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary-inflationary pressure, which erodes real purchasing power and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a disinflationary policy shift.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary behavior, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a consumption rebound.

mechanism_narrative: A positive interaction between industrial production growth (INDPRO > 0.3% MoM) and a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST < previous month) for two months signals a divergence between manufacturing strength and housing weakness, which historically precedes equity market corrections over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.3% MoM AND HOUST < previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a synchronized economic expansion.
